summary: An approval decision whose acknowledgment is lost is treated as not sent: the sequence is not consumed and the card re-enables both buttons, unlike typed input, which retires the credential on uncertainty.
failure_scenario: User clicks Approve; the server applies it (decide_approval advances _last_approval_sequence to N) but the fetch rejects (network drop/proxy reset) or returns non-ok after the effect. ApprovalDecisionController.#dispatch only commits this.sequence after send() resolves, so the browser still holds N-1; submitApproval resets pendingDecision and shows 'Decision failed. Try again.' with Approve/Reject enabled. Reject (or any other approval card) is then sent with sequence N, which is neither the replay of (N, id, approve) nor N+1, so session.decide_approval raises 'approval sequence is not the next expected value'. The opposite decision is lost, and every later approval from this browser carries the stale sequence and is refused until the controller is reset by a reconnect/rebind. Only a byte-identical retry is accepted.
evidence: Read web/src/main.ts:438-463 (sender has no uncertainty handling), web/src/controller.ts ApprovalDecisionController.submit/#dispatch (sequence committed only after success), main.ts submitApproval catch (re-enables controls), src/hermes_realtime/client/session.py decide_approval (replay only on exact tuple, else requires last+1), and contrasted with submitTyped (main.ts:3825+) which disconnects on any uncertain failure. web/tests/review-regressions.test.ts:156 ('still allows a retry after a failed decision') pins retry of [1,approve] then [1,reject], so it encodes the divergent-decision retry. Static trace only; no browser or server run (JS/Python deps not installable offline).

summary: socket.inet_aton fallback accepts trailing whitespace-separated garbage and short numeric forms, so canonical_remote_hostname silently rewrites invalid input to a different address, with platform-dependent behaviour.
failure_scenario: canonical_remote_hostname('8.8.8.8 evil', boundary='b') returns '8.8.8.8'; '1.2.3.4\x0bz' returns '1.2.3.4'; '1' returns '0.0.0.1'. The glibc inet_aton stops at whitespace. Callers that only use the call as a validity check on an unfiltered string (host_launcher.py:2082 browser_host in remote mode) accept a host string that is not a valid hostname; the later bind fails. Callers in runtime.py and host_launcher._validate_livekit_origin pre-filter characters outside 33..126, so the reachable consequence is limited to fail-late validation.
evidence: Ran the function under /usr/bin/python3.11 (project requires >=3.11,<3.12) with the inputs above and observed the outputs. Checked callers in runtime.py:309/331, host_launcher.py:1009/1098/2082. The downstream bind failure was not run.

summary: BrowserBootstrapApplication refuses an http origin on the IPv6 loopback even though the runtime and server accept host '::1' and derive 'http://[::1]:port'.
failure_scenario: Launch with browser_host='::1' without TLS: runtime.py:342-348 builds origin 'http://[::1]:PORT' and client/server.py:136 accepts the host; BrowserBootstrapApplication.__init__ then evaluates urlsplit(origin).hostname == '::1', which is not in {'127.0.0.1','localhost'}, and raises ValueError('non-loopback browser origins require HTTPS'). The mode is advertised by the lower layers but fails at startup (fail-closed, no security impact).
evidence: Confirmed urlsplit('http://[::1]:8765').hostname == '::1' with stdlib and read runtime.py/server.py/http.py. Did not construct the application because pydantic and other dependencies are unavailable offline.

summary: The setup script refuses any existing target but creates the venv before the hashed installs and the CUDA assertion, so a failed install leaves a half-built target that every rerun refuses.
failure_scenario: uv venv succeeds, then a hashed uv pip install or the onnxruntime-gpu/CUDAExecutionProvider assertion fails (network, wheel hash mismatch, missing CUDA). The directory remains, so the next run exits 2 with 'refusing to replace existing CUDA worker environment' until the user deletes it by hand; the script also uses 'pwd -W', which exists only in Git Bash on Windows.
evidence: Read the 19-line script; control flow is set -e with an unconditional -e test at line 10 and uv venv at line 15. Not executed (Windows-only requirements files, no GPU).

summary: VoiceCompanionService.review emits a refusal marker only for the 'unbound' case; other refusals and generic failures return with no evidence line, contrary to the repository rule to record refusals in a finally.
failure_scenario: A review request refused with not_ready or tombstoned, or failing with an exception (returns None), produces no [voice-companion] line, while forget() and archive-open failures do emit one. Review refusal categories are invisible to diagnostics.
evidence: Read host.py review(): evidence is assigned only at line 393 and the except ArchiveRefusal and except Exception branches do not set it. Compared with forget() (marker on every refusal and failure).

summary: Coverage: read in full src/hermes_realtime/{network_origin,client/task_proposal_control,client/http,conversation/telemetry,companion/host,integration/completion,providers/__init__,providers/_text_segmentation,providers/_work_claims,speech/__init__}.py, scripts/qualification_launch.py, setup-kokoro script, lookup manifest, vitest config, web/tests/review-regressions.test.ts, tests/providers/test_codex_task_authority.py and the test_work_claims and test_text_segmentation files; read web/src/main.ts for task cards, approval cards, public-event polling, projection resync, typed input, speech yield and approval sender (about 1,500 of 4,168 lines). No pytest run: uv could not fetch dependencies offline; only stdlib reproductions were used.

Sound after inspection: nearest_rank_percentile matches the exact integer nearest-rank for q in {0.5,0.9,0.95,0.99} for n<5000 (brute-force); HermesCompletionRouter dedupes by run_id with equality-bound re-track and eviction coupled to the dispatch cache callback; canonical_remote_hostname rejects loopback, unspecified and mapped-IPv6 loopback forms and glibc short forms like 0x7f.1 on 3.11; http.py enforces exact methods, origin, content-length, strict JSON with duplicate-key refusal and per-route byte bounds; web projection requires contiguous event sequences and the server always emits task_state before task_result, so the empty-text early return in projectTaskResult cannot strand a card; task proposal decisions reserve the sequence before awaiting and replay exactly; host.py profile-lock handoff, memory stream wakeups and close/quiescence paths showed no defect.

Coverage gap: not reviewed in depth: src/hermes_realtime/evidence/admission.py (5,364 lines; only ConversationOperationScheduler and BoundedEvidenceWriterQueueV1 were read), tests/providers/test_codex_app_server.py (5,131 lines), tests/client/test_task_proposal_control.py, tests/test_qualification_launch.py, tests/conversation/test_telemetry.py and the three web DOM test files beyond the approval retry cases. The Windows Job/kernel behaviour in qualification_launch.py (cleanup member retention, kernel handle closure order, controller exit semantics) was reviewed statically only and cannot be confirmed on Linux. No mutation proofs were run. Not reported as defects: first_speakable_sentence_end and the background-work claim regex use ASCII-only terminators and a finite phrase list (documented as a bounded guard).
